title: The Encirclement Net
text: “Ohh? Are you really that worried about Naofumi-chan? Should Big Sister get a little jealous, hmm?”
Older Sister was teasing away. Even I could tell that Older Sister didn’t mean a single word of it when she talked like that.
“Well… I think Sadeena-san and Elmelo-san could both do well too. Though… Panda would definitely be a valuable addition if we ever wanted a circus act.”
Father went on to say that Elephant, Panda, lions, cheetahs, and horses all had a certain circus-like flair to them.
“So Elmelo-chan’s a good fit too.”
“For now, yes. There’s a more dynamic way to push Elmelo-san further, but… right now she’s split between the ‘caged beast’ exhibit and performing tricks alongside the Filolials in the show.”
“Given her species, well-dressed customers occasionally take a swing at her, though.”

Elephant answered with a wry little laugh. Any customer rude enough to try that got a stern warning from me, I say. It seemed that former soldiers and officers who’d fought in the war against Siltvelt knew all too well how dangerous Elephant could be.

“Well… listening to the tall tales the Siltvelt side tells in front of my cage about their glorious retreat—it’s in poor taste, certainly, but somehow it doesn’t leave me feeling bad to hear it. So it’s not all bad.”
Elephant let out a soft, knowing chuckle.
“You okay with that, Elmelo-san?”
“Yes. When I hear how the very same men who boast so proudly are spoken of on the Melromarc side, comparing how the facts get twisted along the way is rather entertaining.”

Apparently this was about the mammoth folk back home in Elephant’s village. No doubt some noble had been spinning a heroic tale in front of Elephant about the time the mammoths were routed. Incidentally, Elephant apparently understood a bit of the Melromarc language—enough to catch the gist, even if only in fragments.
“That’s… a bit dark, honestly. Elmelo-san, if it ever really bothers you, just say so. I’ll deal with it as best I can.”
“There is no issue. If anything, I worry more that Kou-san and the other Filolials might get hurt. It’s been quite a task calming Kou-san down whenever he gets upset at the customers’ attitude.”

Elephant truly had a generous heart, I say. And it was reassuring to know Kou was coming along nicely under her guidance. Apparently he’d been booing in protest whenever some noble spun an insult disguised as a war story at Elephant. Thankfully, it seemed he’d avoided turning timid from being scolded by Father. Either way, for the sake of Father’s circus expansion plan—and, more importantly, for my own ambition of letting Yuki-chan race on the lawn track at the circus—there was much to be done. Most unwillingly, I supposed I’d have to entrust the bio-plants to Lazy Pig.
“Anyway, a panda, huh…”
“No doubt she’d be excellent material for the act—nimble hands, great at leaping about. Not to mention she’s quite good with numbers, I say.”
“I get that she’d be perfect for scouting, but there’s no getting around the fact that we don’t have one…”
Tch! The sting of my failed scouting attempt still lingered. I’d been certain that if Father himself made the offer, it’d be a done deal.
“Now that I think of it, apparently there’s someone from Panda’s hometown living in the castle town. Shall we go have a word with them? We’ll need to track them down first, though.”
Where on earth would they even be running a shop, I wondered.
“You mean Lars has relatives here?”
Apparently Elephant hadn’t known that either.
“Hmm…”
“Or perhaps we could head straight to Panda’s home village instead?”
I did have a Portal on hand, so we could get there in a flash.
“Motoyasu-kun, you seem to know a suspicious amount about this person.”
“Father and I have crossed paths so many times it’s practically fate by this point, I say. I’ve got their whole family situation memorized from the loops.”

Come to think of it, I really did need to arrange an introduction between Trash and Tiger Girl—the daughter of Panda’s first love. But with the Crimson Swine currently residing in Melromarc’s castle, showing her off there was clearly out of the question. I recalled how even Siltvelt’s envoy had worn a sour expression, uneasy about a member of Tiger Girl’s race falling under Father’s banner. If the Crimson Swine ever learned of Tiger Girl’s existence, she wouldn’t hesitate for a second before plotting her murder. Even I wouldn’t stoop to something so vile. First, I’d see to the Crimson Swine’s removal—then present Tiger Girl to Trash and crush what fighting spirit he had left.
“Lars… there’s no escaping it, is there. Just how much do you know about me?”
“Ohh?”
“For that matter, I know everything about Elephant’s family too, I say.”
“Ugh… please, I beg you, don’t say anything.”
Oh dear, Elephant had stopped me cold. And here I’d been about to turn it into quite the heroic tale.
“Well, Elephant’s family matters can wait until Melromarc’s affairs are settled, I say.”
“Please, just stop…”
“Elmelo-chan, that sounds rough. Big Sister’s awfully something, isn’t she?”
“Older Sister was busy looking for Big Sister, I say.”
“Ohh, is that really the only thing you’ve got?”
“Nothing else, no.”
“Ohh, is that so. Well, Big Sister’s glad she never had such a rough past like Elmelo-chan’s.”
“You…”

Elephant stared at Older Sister with a look of pure exasperation. Come to think of it, I never really understood Older Sister all that well. All I knew was that she’d been close with Big Sister’s parents once.
“Now, now… Motoyasu-kun genuinely means well toward Elmelo-san, so I don’t think he’d ever actually do anything to trouble her, right?”
“I do hope that’s the case…”
“Anyway, Motoyasu-kun. You said you know where this panda person’s home is—is it actually safe to go there?”
“No problem at all, I say. Panda’s grandfather currently wields ki even more powerfully than Panda herself. Scouting the grandfather in her place is also an option, I say.”
Would you cut that out already! Panda seemed to protest inside my head, but that was surely just my imagination.
“Panda’s village is full of pandas, I say.”
“Whoa… sounds like a dream destination.”
Father seemed positively delighted at the thought of visiting a village full of pandas.
“Come to think of it, Panda’s grandfather has a long-standing rival in an old woman from Melromarc—whenever the two meet, they happily beat each other senseless, I say.”
“There’s a person like that too? New information just keeps piling up here.”

“Indeed… the old woman makes for an excellent combat advisor in every single loop, I say. She’s currently weakened by illness, but if Father performs a good deed and gets her to drink the medicine, she’ll cooperate wholeheartedly, from the bottom of her heart.”
“Wait, doesn’t that mean, in game terms, my Good Deed Points aren’t high enough to recruit her?”
Oh? Was that actually a possibility?
“Well, curing the illness fully does take a bit of time, but I believe persistence will see it through, I say.”
It seemed that directly curing her illness was itself enough to earn her deep gratitude.
“I’m not too confident about that one… if I go in relying on loop knowledge without care, the recruitment’s probably going to fail.”
“Indeed, given how badly the attempt with Lars went, it’s certainly plausible.”
Ngh… I say.
“That’s true. Even after Motoyasu-kun helped me, trusting him took quite a lot of doing.”
“So what shall we do, then?”
“Um… the panda village does sound kind of interesting. The old woman’s case seems like it needs good deeds first, but for the panda, maybe just talking with the daughter directly would work out.”
“Well, I think Lars will take the job as long as you pile on enough gold. It’s really just that she misunderstood the Spear Hero-sama’s negotiation tactics.”
“Motoyasu-kun, exactly what kind of negotiation did you do?”
“Nothing at all out of the ordinary, I say.”
“No… it came across more like elder care—including in a rather sexual sense, if I’m being honest.”
What, my recruitment pitch had been taken that way? Now that I thought about it, Panda had indeed given some rather suggestive-sounding responses at the time.
“Motoyasu-kun. Did you introduce me as some sort of elderly man? Or rather, what exactly did you say to this panda person about me…”
“It’s a misunderstanding, I say.”
“The real issue was how Spear Hero-sama referred to Shield Hero-sama.”

“Ah… I see, that would explain it if you don’t know the context. I thought so too… and she kept pressing me rather persistently about my virginity, so now I’m a little suspicious about whether it really was just a misunderstanding.”
Father had drifted off into some sort of melancholy for reasons unknown. Regardless, I couldn’t afford to let my reputation sink any further!
“Well then, shall we at least go and pay our respects?”
“Sure, even just as a traveler passing through by chance is fine—I’d like to see it. Panda’s village.”
“Understood. Then let us depart, I say.”
